title: rorca-subprocess-watchdog

userStories.title: Extract createIdleWatchdog shared helper function
userStories.description: Create a shared helper function `createIdleWatchdog` in `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts` that encapsulates all idle timeout logic. The function accepts a child process, timeout duration in ms (from `LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` env var with default 300000), and a log callback for emitting visible error messages. It returns `{ reset(), clear() }` — `reset()` clears and restarts the idle timer, `clear()` tears down the timer permanently. This is the foundation all three spawn functions will use.
acceptanceCriteria: Function `createIdleWatchdog(child, timeoutMs, onFire)` exists and is callable from within execution-engine.ts
`LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` env var is read with `parseInt(process.env.LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS ?? '', 10)` and falls back to 300000 if missing or NaN — no hardcoded values anywhere else
`reset()` calls `clearTimeout` on the previous timer and starts a new `setTimeout` for `timeoutMs` ms
`clear()` calls `clearTimeout` unconditionally and sets the internal timer reference to undefined so it cannot fire after clear
`onFire` callback is invoked by the watchdog before SIGTERM — allows caller to inject log lines before the process is killed

suggestedSkills.name: logging-fundamentals
suggestedSkills.reason: onFire callback pattern is the log injection point — proper structured logging matters here

userStories.title: Wire createIdleWatchdog into all three spawn functions
userStories.description: Update `spawnClaude`, `spawnOpenCode`, and `spawnCodex` in `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts` to use `createIdleWatchdog`. Each spawn function must: (1) call `createIdleWatchdog` after the child process is created, passing `LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` and a log callback that writes a visible `[System] Watchdog triggered: No output received for N minutes. Killing process...` line into the terminal output stream; (2) call `watchdog.reset()` inside both `child.stdout.on('data')` and `child.stderr.on('data')` handlers; (3) call `watchdog.clear()` inside `child.on('close')`, `child.on('exit')`, AND `child.on('error')` handlers — all three, not just close. The existing 45-minute wall-clock `setTimeout` stays as a safety net and is also cleared in all three event handlers.
acceptanceCriteria: All three spawn functions (`spawnClaude`, `spawnOpenCode`, `spawnCodex`) call `createIdleWatchdog` immediately after child process creation
`watchdog.reset()` is called in both `stdout.on('data')` and `stderr.on('data')` handlers — confirmed by code inspection
`watchdog.clear()` is called in `child.on('close')`, `child.on('exit')`, AND `child.on('error')` in all three spawn functions — all three event handlers, not just `close`
The existing 45-minute wall-clock `setTimeout` is also cleared in `close`, `exit`, and `error` handlers (additive cleanup — both timers cleaned)
The `onFire` log callback writes a line matching pattern `[System] Watchdog triggered: No output received for N minutes. Killing process...` into the same stream as normal agent output

userStories.title: Classify idle_timeout in WAL events and retry logic
userStories.description: When the watchdog fires and sends SIGTERM, the process exit handler must distinguish idle timeout from wall-clock timeout and from other non-zero exits. Add an `idleTimedOut` flag (set to true in the `onFire` callback before SIGTERM) so the exit handler can emit a WAL event with `reason: 'idle_timeout'` instead of the generic `reason: 'timeout'` used for the 45-minute wall-clock kill. The existing MAX_RETRIES=3 retry logic and model escalation must apply to `idle_timeout` exits identically to other failures — no special-casing that bypasses retries.
acceptanceCriteria: A boolean `idleTimedOut` flag is set to `true` in the `onFire` callback before SIGTERM is sent, and is readable by the exit handler via closure
WAL event emitted on idle timeout has `payload.reason === 'idle_timeout'` — distinct from `reason: 'timeout'` (wall-clock) and `reason: 'max_retries'`
Idle timeout exits trigger the same retry path as other non-zero exits — `retryCount` increments, model escalation applies if OpenCode, story is not marked failed until MAX_RETRIES exhausted
`npx tsc --noEmit` in `backend/` passes with no new errors after this change
TypeScript type for the WAL event reason union includes `'idle_timeout'` alongside existing values

suggestedSkills.name: observability-logging
suggestedSkills.reason: WAL event classification is the observability signal operators use to diagnose silent hangs

suggestedSkills.name: assumption-buster
suggestedSkills.reason: Retry logic assumptions — does idle_timeout count as a retryable error? — need explicit validation

userStories.title: Integration test: watchdog fires, logs, and triggers retry
userStories.description: Write a Jest integration test in `backend/src/lib/__tests__/idle-watchdog.test.ts` (or alongside existing execution-engine tests) that verifies the end-to-end idle watchdog behavior without spawning a real LLM. Mock or stub the child process: emit no stdout/stderr for `timeoutMs` ms, then assert that (a) SIGTERM was sent to the child, (b) the visible log line was emitted, and (c) the retry counter incremented. Also test the cleanup path: emit one data event before the timeout, confirm SIGTERM was NOT sent. Test that `clear()` after `child.on('error')` prevents a dangling timer from firing.
acceptanceCriteria: Test file `backend/src/lib/__tests__/idle-watchdog.test.ts` exists and runs via `cd backend && npx jest --testPathPattern=idle-watchdog`
Test case: child emits no data for `timeoutMs` → SIGTERM sent → log line matching `/\[System\] Watchdog triggered/` appears in captured output
Test case: child emits one data event at t=0, then silence — SIGTERM must NOT fire before `timeoutMs` elapses from the last data event (reset on data is working)
Test case: `child.on('error')` fires before idle timeout → `clear()` is called → watchdog never fires (no dangling timer)
`npx tsc --noEmit` in `backend/` passes after adding the test file, and `npm test` exits 0

suggestedSkills.reason: This story is entirely about making implicit timer behavior explicit and tested

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Add an idle stream timeout (subprocess watchdog) to Rorca's execution engine. Currently, all three agent spawn functions (spawnClaude, spawnOpenCode, spawnCodex) in backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts use a fixed 45-minute wall-clock timeout via setTimeout. If an LLM provider hangs silently (e.g., Anthropic returns a 500 and the CLI sits frozen), Rorca waits the full 45 minutes before killing the process. This wastes time and blocks the pipeline.

The fix: add an idle timer that resets every time stdout or stderr emits data. If no output arrives within a configurable window (default 5 minutes, configurable via LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable), the watchdog fires SIGTERM immediately, triggering the existing retry logic.

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS that must be acceptance criteria:

1. Comprehensive Timer Cleanup: clearTimeout(idleTimer) must fire on child.on('close'), child.on('exit'), AND child.on('error') — not just on successful completion. Dangling timers keep the Node.js event loop alive and will eventually crash the worker process. This is the single biggest risk.

2. Standardized Timeout Variable: The idle timeout MUST be pulled from environment variable LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS with a sensible default (300000ms = 5 minutes). No hardcoded values.

3. Explicit Log Emitting: When the watchdog fires, it MUST inject a visible error line into the terminal output stream (e.g., "[System] Watchdog triggered: No output received for 5 minutes. Killing process...") so operators see WHY attempt 1 failed. Silent SIGTERM is not acceptable.

4. The existing wall-clock timeout (45 min) stays as a safety net. The idle timer is additive. Both timers must be cleaned up on process exit.

5. The idle timer must reset on BOTH stdout AND stderr data events.

6. Error classification must distinguish idle timeout from wall-clock timeout. WAL event should include reason: 'idle_timeout'. Existing retry logic (MAX_RETRIES=3, model escalation) applies to idle timeouts same as other failures.

Architecture: Extract watchdog logic into a shared helper function (e.g., createIdleWatchdog) that returns { reset(), clear() } and takes the child process + timeout config. Avoid copy-pasting into each spawn function.
